sections.name: architecture layering
sections.title: Layering rule checks
sections.what: Checks the real source has no violations, the bad fixture gives exactly three violations with clear messages, and sample imports follow the allowed and forbidden rules.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the layers separate so changes stay contained.
sections.watch_out: The messages are matched as text, so editing wording breaks the test.

summary: Tests the code layering rules: the real source folder must be clean, the bad fixture must produce exactly three violations with helpful messages, and the import rules must work as described.
purpose: Keeps the codebase structured so each layer depends only on the layers it should.
why: Likely reason: clear layers make changes safer and keep business logic away from the user interface and the database.
how: Checks the real source folder has no layering problems. Checks the bad fixture produces three named violations with messages about moving shared code, pure engine I/O, and UI database access. Checks sample import lines against the rules: allowed forward dependencies pass, cross-domain repository access fails, and provider and app imports fail.
inputs: The source folder, the fixture folder and sample import lines.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test.
risks: The root is the current working folder, so running from elsewhere changes results. Messages are matched by pattern, so rewording a message breaks the test.
debug: If the source check fails, the failure lists the file and message. If a rule test fails, compare the sample import with the rule text.
